record.explanation: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy classically manifests with postural hypotension (cardiovascular), urinary retention (genitourinary), and diarrhoea (gastrointestinal - 'diabetic diarrhoea' from enteric neuropathy/bacterial overgrowth). While constipation can occur, recurrent diarrhoea is the hallmark GI feature; constipation is less specific and less emphasized as a direct sign of autonomic neuropathy in standard teaching.

record.question: Appropriate anaesthetic management for ophthalmic surgery requires tight control of intraocular pressure (IOP) before, during, and after the procedure. The accurate effect of an anaesthetic drug on IOP is
record.explanation: Hyperventilation (hypocapnia) reliably decreases IOP via choroidal vasoconstriction, so option (b) is incorrect. Nondepolarizing muscle relaxants do not increase IOP (they avoid succinylcholine-induced rises). Glycopyrrolate, an anticholinergic, can increase IOP in narrow-angle glaucoma and does not decrease it. Nitrous oxide has minimal effect on IOP in normal eyes; some older literature reports a slight decrease, making this the only option not definitively false across all sources, though modern texts describe no significant effect.

options: Airways such as the laryngeal mask airway and oesophageal obturator airway are always useful in the event of a failed airway.
Awake intubation may be done by the nasotracheal route.
Care should be taken before intubation to assess the airway for ease of ventilation as well as intubation.
Cricothyrotomy is the crucial rescue procedure when intubation and ventilation fail.
appearance.subject: gk
appearance.canonical_answer_text: Airways such as the laryngeal mask airway and oesophageal obturator airway are always useful in the event of a failed airway.

record.question: After rapid sequence induction of general anaesthesia, a patient is unable to be intubated. Subsequent attempts at ventilation by face mask and a supraglottic airway device are also unsuccessful. One of the following statements regarding transtracheal jet ventilation and surgical cricothyrotomy in this situation is most correct
options: Transtracheal jet ventilation does not require a patent natural airway
Ventilation through a surgical cricothyrotomy allows both inhalation and exhalation to occur
The development of laryngospasm during ventilation through a cricothyrotomy would rapidly cause pulmonary over inflation and barotrauma
Transtracheal jet ventilation can be continued for a longer period of time than can ventilation via a cricothyrotomy
